solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Charge about, arresting one or two

indicators.note: arresting means holding, so one piece is held inside the other
about tells us to turn the word for charge round, back to front

parts.note: to rap someone is to charge or accuse them
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A police officer rushes around, arresting one or two suspects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns RAP into PAR, and 'arresting' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple or twosome is a set of two, and so is a matching duo.

clue.text: Picture of seaside town, artist taking it

parts.note: a port is a town on the coast
RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts in London

explanation.surface: A painting of a harbour town, with the painter taking it on.
explanation.definitionFit: A painted or photographed likeness of a person is a kind of picture.

clue.text: I have endless stock, and add in new?

definitions.text: I have endless stock, and add in new?

indicators.note: add in tells us to slip one piece inside the rest

parts.note: I have is shortened to I've

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the word for stock is dropped

parts.note: a store is a stock or supply

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of a big stockpile while still asking to put in more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' and 'add in' are the two signals. The whole clue is also the definition: a shareholder talking about putting fresh money in.
explanation.definitionFit: A shareholder owns stock and puts fresh money into a business, which is just what the speaker describes.

clue.text: Rascal sticks pin into gangster but without force

indicators.note: sticks, read with into, says one piece is pushed inside another
into finishes the instruction, saying where the pin goes
without means the letter for force is taken away

parts.note: Scarface was the nickname of the Chicago gangster Al Capone
F is the abbreviation for force in physics
a peg is a pin used to fasten or hang things

explanation.surface: A villain stabs a mobster with a pin, but gently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' makes SCARACE, which 'sticks...into' opens up. Most solvers look for AL as the gangster; here it is Al Capone's nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: A scapegrace is a scamp or good-for-nothing, the same sort of mischief-maker as a rascal.

clue.text: Moving quietly up, steal fabric

indicators.note: Moving says one letter changes its place within the word
in a down clue up means the letter shifts towards the top, one place earlier

parts.note: to steal along is to creep
P stands for piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A thief creeps silently upward to pinch some cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving...up' shifts the P in CREEP one place higher, which gives CREPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Crepe is a thin crinkled cloth, so it is a type of fabric.

clue.text: Son wearing fairy cloak that gives a superior look

indicators.note: the son is wrapped in the clothing, so his letter sits inside the rest

parts.note: a peri is a fairy in Persian myth
a cope is a long cloak worn by a priest

explanation.surface: A boy dressed in a fairy costume gets a lofty view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' signals the container. 'superior' is meant literally here: higher up.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine's periscope lets the viewer see from a higher point, a look from above.

clue.text: Revolutionary act well before the Boston Tea Party?

definitions.text: Revolutionary act well before the Boston Tea Party?

parts.words: Revolutionary act well before the Boston Tea Party?
parts.note: the 1605 plot to blow up Parliament was a revolutionary act long before the 1773 Boston protest that helped start the American Revolution

explanation.surface: A history question about an uprising earlier than the American one.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1605 Guy Fawkes and others planned to blow up the English Parliament. The Boston Tea Party came in 1773.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1605 conspiracy aimed to overthrow King James I, so it was a revolutionary act more than 150 years before Boston.

clue.text: A Guernsey detective cut off sharpish

parts.note: Guernsey is one of the Channel Islands, abbreviated CI

indicators.note: cut off means the last letter of the word for detective is dropped

parts.note: dick is slang for a detective

explanation.surface: A Guernsey police officer is cut short rather abruptly.
explanation.definitionFit: An acidic taste is sour and tart, so sharpish describes it.

clue.text: Book advises the right clothes

indicators.note: clothes means the words wrap around the letters we want

explanation.surface: A guide advises the right outfits to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' signals letters held inside 'advisES THE Right'.
explanation.definitionFit: Esther is one of the books of the Old Testament in the Bible.

clue.text: During worship I dream

indicators.note: During puts the I inside the word for worship

parts.note: to revere is to worship

explanation.surface: Someone drifts off in a daydream while at a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverie is a daydream, a state of absent musing.

clue.text: Series of talks from heretic result in chaos

indicators.note: in chaos says the letters of the two words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A heretic's lectures end in disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: The Reith Lectures are an annual series of radio talks broadcast by the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC's yearly radio lectures, named after Lord Reith, form a series of public talks.

clue.text: Little chap drinks port to grow massively

indicators.note: drinks means takes in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a runt is an undersized person
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A small boy downs port and then shoots up.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants that grow out of control are said to spread wildly, an idiom for growing without check.

clue.text: User isn't bothered by salesman's initial lack of practice

indicators.note: bothered means upset, so the letters are stirred up
initial means just the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A customer is not bothered by an unskilled salesman.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out of practice leaves your skills stiff and dulled, like metal left to corrode.

clue.text: Arch charity worker's plea

definitions.meaning: a pointed Gothic arch, or a diagonal rib in a vault
read as two words, '...!' is a fundraiser's appeal

explanation.surface: A volunteer collector makes an arch appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arch' looks like an adjective (mischievous) describing the plea, but it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: In architecture an ogive is a pointed arch or a vaulting rib.

clue.text: To explain (a phrase she didn't use): I must come first

indicators.note: must come first places I at the front

parts.note: a phrase she did not say is not her words

explanation.surface: A writer, explaining, swaps in their own phrasing for one she never said.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as I + NOT HER WORDS.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces a restatement put more simply, so it is used to clarify.

clue.text: Being king, suppressing rising in turn is very unattractive

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down, so the word for rising is kept inside

parts.note: regnant means reigning

indicators.note: in turn tells us to flip the word for rising back to front

parts.note: rising means going up

explanation.surface: A reigning monarch crushing an uprising is a nasty sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in turn' signals the reversal, and 'suppressing' holds the result inside, just after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repugnant is repulsive or disgusting, far worse than merely plain.

clue.text: I think, and I write what I think here?

definitions.text: I write what I think here?
definitions.meaning: taken literally, a diary or notebook where my thoughts are written down

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: inside my own notebook.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in my view, and literally names one's own written volume.

clue.text: Inside mountain, radius taken

indicators.note: Inside puts the word for radius within the word for mountain

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
a spoke is a radius of a wheel

explanation.surface: Inside a mountain, someone has taken a radius measurement.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone already spoken for or engaged is taken, which is the old sense of bespoken.

clue.text: What bestows second sight?

parts.note: second sight suggests clairvoyance, but here it is simply seeing someone a second time when they show up again

explanation.walkthrough: 'second sight' looks like psychic power; it means a second look at someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning up again lets people see you a second time.

clue.text: Briefly on fire, Roman priest almost smothers bishop

indicators.note: smothers means covers up, so the letter for bishop goes inside
almost means the last letter of the word for the priest is dropped

parts.note: a flamen was a priest of one god in ancient Rome
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A Roman priest, briefly in flames, smothers a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts FLAMEN to FLAME, and 'smothers' puts B inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish served flambéed has brandy poured over and set alight for a moment.

clue.text: What my pet loves: a drink of milk and a piece of cake brought up

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means the letters are read from the bottom upward

parts.note: pinta is British slang for a pint of milk

indicators.note: a piece of means only the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A pet owner lists favourite treats: milk and a slice of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns PINTAC round. The pet is taken to be a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Cats are famously drawn to this herb, so it is what a pet cat loves.

clue.text: Rose suddenly turned pale and finally wept

indicators.note: turned means the letters are switched around
finally takes just the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Rose went white and in the end cried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a woman's name; it is the past tense of rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To jump is to rise suddenly; the past tense matches rose.

clue.text: Fail to leave ring? Yes

parts.note: to go is to leave
to bell is to ring
yup is a casual yes

explanation.surface: A boxer is asked whether he failed to get out of the ring and says yes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, taken from a dead fish floating, means a business collapses or fails.

clue.text: Congratulations for assassin

definitions.meaning: a hired killer, an old sense from Italian

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a cheer of well done and also an old term for a hired killer.

clue.text: After a short time, about to turn against a goddess

indicators.note: After puts the rest following the short time

parts.note: min is short for a minute

indicators.note: to turn means the word for about is read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning
V stands for versus, against

explanation.surface: After a brief pause, someone is about to turn against a goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Minerva was the Roman goddess of wisdom.

clue.text: Statue perhaps of couple with king stored in chest

indicators.note: stored in means placed inside the word for chest

parts.note: an ark is a chest or box
a couple is two
R stands for rex, king

explanation.surface: A pair of statues and a king are packed away in a chest.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is one example of a piece of art, so 'perhaps' marks it.

clue.text: Setting out from old place

parts.note: ex means former
a position is a place

explanation.surface: Setting out from an old place.
explanation.definitionFit: An exposition is a laying-out of facts or a full account, a setting forth.

clue.text: Almost broke surface

indicators.note: Almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: skint is British slang for broke

explanation.walkthrough: SKINT is British slang for having no money.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer layer of a body or a fruit is its covering, its surface.
